citation.authors: Schwander F, Kopf-Bolanz KA, Buri C, Portmann R, Egger L, Chollet M, McTernan PG, Piya MK, Gijs MAM, Vionnet N, Pralong F, Laederach K, Vergères G
citation.title: A Dose-Response Strategy Reveals Differences between Normal-Weight and Obese Men in Their Metabolic and Inflammatory Responses to a High-Fat Meal

population.description: Men aged 25-55 y (enrolment criterion) from the region of Berne: 19 normal-weight (BMI 20-25 kg/m2, waist <94 cm) and 18 obese (BMI >30, waist >102 cm) were enrolled; one obese man was excluded from the analyses because his baseline glucose, insulin and TGs rose during the study, so Tables 2 and 3 give n = 19 and n = 17 (36 analysed). Exclusions: cardiovascular disease, diagnosed diabetes, inflammatory condition, relevant medication, smoking, food allergy, impaired kidney or liver function. No glucose tolerance test was reported, so both groups are unselected; the paper reports all obese men but one had HOMA-IR above 2.6. Age and BMI are given per group (Table 2, means ± SD) in each protocol's override; no pooled values are printed, so the top level carries none.

protocols.name: fasted_nw
protocols.description: Fasting blood sample of the normal-weight men, drawn between 08:00 and 09:00 after a 10-h overnight fast before a test meal (Table 2 does not say which of the 3 study mornings it prints, or whether it averages them; each was this same 10-h-fasted 08:00-09:00 t = 0 sample, and the paper says the baseline values remained stable throughout the study); a 30-min fasted run-in, no food (start_hour 8.5 is the midpoint of the printed 08:00-09:00 interval)

protocols.name: meal_500_nw
protocols.description: Normal-weight men, high-fat test meal A (500 kcal: bread, palm fat, sausage, boiled eggs; Table 1: 26.3 g carbohydrate, 34.0 g fat, 22.7 g protein) after a 10-h overnight fast, blood between 08:00 and 09:00 at t = 0 (start of the meal) and 1, 2, 4, 6 h; meal entered at minute 0, its eating time not printed; start_hour 8.5 is the midpoint of 08:00-09:00. Meal details (Methods, Table 1): the foods are bread (58 g), palm fat (13 g), sausage (52 g; 'salami' in Methods) and boiled eggs (26 g); the added fat is palm fat; protein from bread 5.8 g, sausage 13.5 g and boiled eggs 3.4 g, entered as mixed; 200 mL Vittel water drunk with the meal carries no grams, so the form is solid

meals.food: bread, palm fat, salami and boiled eggs

protocols.name: meal_1000_nw
protocols.description: Normal-weight men, high-fat test meal B (1000 kcal), after a 10-h overnight fast, blood between 08:00 and 09:00 at t = 0 (start of the meal) and 1, 2, 4, 6 h. Grams derived from energy and percentages of energy: the paper says the 3 meals had the same macronutrient composition (Table 1 footnote: same composition, 2 times the calories of meal A; Table 1: 21.3% carbohydrate, 60.5% fat, 18.2% protein), so carbohydrate 1000 x 0.213 / 4 = 53.25 g, fat 1000 x 0.605 / 9 = 67.22 g, protein 1000 x 0.182 / 4 = 45.5 g; meal entered at minute 0, its eating time not printed; start_hour 8.5 is the midpoint of 08:00-09:00. Meal details (Methods, Table 1 and footnote): the same foods as meal A, bread, palm fat, sausage ('salami' in Methods) and boiled eggs; the added fat is palm fat; protein from bread, sausage and boiled eggs, entered as mixed; 400 mL Vittel water drunk with the meal carries no grams, so the form is solid
